questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that the right lane will end.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Allows you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
Can become a hazard to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: DOT-approved helmets do not limit your vision. They allow you to see everything you need for safe riding.

questions.question: Your lane position while riding a motorcycle:

options.text: Has little impact on whether other drivers can see you.
Is very important because it affects whether other drivers can see you.
Cannot protect you from wind blasts from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is very important because it affects whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Your position in the lane is important. It helps you see better and helps other drivers see you. Good positioning also protects you from wind from other vehicles.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should wear:

options.text: Bright-colored clothing to be more visible.
Clothing of any color because drivers can see you easily in daylight.
Dark-colored clothing to stand out against the bright sun.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright-colored clothing to be more visible.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Always wear bright-colored clothing to stay visible, even in daylight.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Use the rear brake before the front brake.

questions.explanation: For a quick stop, use the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: If you have one drink before riding:

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
It can affect your ability to ride a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can affect your ability to ride a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Your riding skills are affected by the first drink. Do not ride if you have consumed any alcohol.

questions.question: Should you wear gloves while riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Yes. Your hands may get cold while riding.
Yes. They give you a better grip and protect your hands.
No. Gloves are not recommended because they interfere with controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes. They give you a better grip and protect your hands.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip and protect your hands. Use full-fingered gloves made of strong material.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to turn red.
The traffic light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A yellow traffic light warns that it will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through it.

questions.question: You can be seen more easily at an intersection by:
questions.explanation: Use your headlight at all times of day. This helps other drivers see you at intersections.

questions.question: As your motorcycle accelerates, you will need to:
questions.explanation: As your motorcycle accelerates, shift into a higher gear.

questions.question: Locking your brakes can:
questions.explanation: Locking your brakes causes you to lose control. If your front brake locks, release it and apply it again. If your rear brake locks on a good surface when stopping, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles that go slower than 25 mph, such as farm equipment or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: Blind spots on motorcycles:

options.text: Should be checked often by riders.
Don't exist if the motorcycle has a mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be checked often by riders.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your regular riding routine.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, focus most on:
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important thing to consider when buying a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: When riding, your feet should be:
questions.explanation: Keep your feet on the footrests while riding. This helps you stay balanced.

questions.question: Your boots or shoes should:
questions.explanation: Choose sturdy shoes or boots that cover and support your ankles. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign with white background and red and black markings. It tells drivers about traffic laws. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a crash, you should:
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others, use your signals, keep safe distance from other vehicles, look ahead at least 12 seconds, identify hazards, and be ready for changes.

questions.question: Texting while driving is:

options.text: Allowed when stopped at traffic lights.

questions.explanation: Texting while driving is very dangerous and increases crash risk by up to 23 times. South Dakota law prohibits texting while operating a vehicle.

questions.question: Mirrors on motorcycles:

options.text: Have blind spots, just like cars.
Don't have blind spots because motorcycles are smaller than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have blind spots, just like cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like cars. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Riding in the left third of the lane lets the driver see you in their side mirror. What is the problem with this position?

options.text: Most drivers check their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror.
Wind can block the side mirror.
Drivers should not use side mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers check their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their side mirrors less often than their rearview mirror. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane. This way, the driver will most likely see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed. Avoid sudden movements and use both brakes when you need to stop.

questions.question: The faster you drink alcohol:

options.text: The faster it leaves your body.
The faster it builds up in your body.
The less it affects your body.

questions.correctAnswerText: The faster it builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the faster alcohol builds up in your body. Your body removes about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your system after that hour.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.explanation: Do not make sudden movements on slippery surfaces. Any quick change in speed or direction can cause you to skid. Move smoothly when speeding up, changing gears, turning, or braking.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to signal the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, if you arrive at the same time as another driver, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.
